chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, altogether from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Qays Abi Ismail, and he mentioned that there is no problem with him from our companions, raising it (to the Prophet).

He said: A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, advise me.' So he said, 'Preserve your tongue.' He said, 'O Messenger of Allah, advise me.' He said, 'Preserve your tongue.' He said, 'O Messenger of Allah, advise me.' He said, 'Preserve your tongue. Woe to you! And what causes people to be thrown on their faces into the Fire except the harvest of their tongues?'

key_terms.مَنَاخِرُهُمْ: Their nostrils/beaks (metaphor for falling on faces)

ai.seo_question: What is the Prophet's repeated advice regarding the tongue?
ai.summary: In this foundational hadith from al-Kafi, the Prophet’s repetition of 'Presive your tongue' underscores its critical role in spiritual preservation, a theme central to Shia ethical teachings on self-discipline. The metaphor of the tongue as a 'harvest' (hasa'id) that casts people into Hellfire highlights how accumulated verbal sins, such as backbiting and idle talk, serve as the primary catalyst for divine punishment. This narration is frequently cited by scholars like Al-Majlisi to emphasize that controlling speech is a prerequisite for controlling one's desires and achieving closeness to God.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibrahim Bin Abdul Hameed, from Qays Abu Ismail, and mentioned that there is no problem with him from our companions, raising it,

‘He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘A man came over to the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> and he said, ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! Advise me’. So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Preserve your tongue’. He said, ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! Advise me. He<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Preserve your tongue’. He said ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>! Advise me’. He<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Preserve your tongue. Woe be unto you! And would the people be flung upon their nostrils into the Fire except due to the harvest of their tongues?’
en.sarwar: 14. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Muhammad ibn Isma’il from Fadl ibn Shadhan all from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Ibrahim ibn ‘Abd al-Hamid from Qays abu Isma’il (he has said that he is fine and is of our people) in a marfu’ manner from the Messenger of Allah, recipient of divine supreme covenant: “

Once a man came to the Holy Prophet and said, ‘O Messenger of Allah, advise me.’ The Messenger of Allah (a.s.) said, ‘Control your tongue.’ He then said, ‘O Messenger of Allah, advise me.’ The Messenger of Allah said, ‘Control your tongue.’ He again said, ‘O Messenger of Allah, advise me.’ The Messenger of Allah said, ‘Control your tongue. Fie upon you, do people get thrown into fire headlong for any reason other than being a victim due to their own tongue?”’
